newsitem.title: USA: Air Force to name two missile contract finalists.
newsitem.headline: Air Force to name two missile contract finalists.

text.p: The Air Force planned to announce two contractor finalists Friday in a $2 billion programme to produce new single-stage space missiles replacing present two-stage Titan, Atlas and Delta missiles.

Announcement of the finalists for the missile now known only as the Evolved Expendable Launch Vehicle was scheduled for 4:30 p.m. EST (2130 GMT). They were to get contracts totalling $120 million or more and one of them is to be selected in about 17 months to manufacture the new missile.

The two finalists were to be selected from four who developed preliminary design proposals for the new missile: Alliant Techsystems Inc., of Magna, Utah; Boeing Defence and Space Group of Seatte, Lockheed Martin Corp.'s Astronautics Division near Denver, and McDonnell Douglas Aerospace of Huntington Beach, Calif.
The Air Force said the new single-stage rocket was part of President Clinton's space transportation plan and will cut the cost of space launches.
"Such consolidation should improve efficiency and lower the costs in a number of areas, such as by using common launch crews and production lines," it said.
Medium and heavy lift versions of the missile will be able to put payloads from about 2,500 pounds to 45,000 pounds into a low earth orbit, the Air force said.

It said the medium lift version is to be ready for its first launches from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California in 2001 and Cape Canaveral in Florida in 2002. The heavy lift version is to begin launches at Vandenberg in 2005 and Cape Canaveral in 2006, it said.
